headline_marked: Controversial audio clip: [[Cantonment Police OC withdrawn]]
headline: Controversial audio clip: Cantonment Police OC withdrawn
summary: Md Rakibul Hasan was attached to DMP headquarters after a viral recording allegedly showed him criticizing the government, the army, and the police force.
details: The officer-in-charge (OC) of Cantonment Police Station, Md Rakibul Hasan, has been withdrawn and attached to the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) headquarters.
The move follows the circulation of an audio clip on social media in which the officer allegedly made controversial remarks about the government, administration, and police.
In the viral recording, a voice allegedly belonging to the OC is heard criticizing the Bangladesh Army, the police force, and the current administration.
The speaker in the clip also claimed that police personnel on the ground are 'very weak' and alleged that senior police officials were leaning towards the BNP.
Furthermore, the audio recording contains allegations of bribery within the police force, claiming that postings are secured through bribes.
Md Aktar Hossain, deputy commissioner (media) of the DMP, confirmed the withdrawal, stating it was done for 'administrative reasons'.
DMP officials have stated that the contents of the audio clip will be examined and further appropriate action will be taken against the OC if necessary.
caption:
A police chief is out after a viral audio clip allegedly leaked his views on the government and the army.

The officer-in-charge (OC) of Cantonment Police Station, Md Rakibul Hasan, has been withdrawn and attached to the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) headquarters.

The move follows the circulation of an audio clip on social media in which the officer allegedly made controversial remarks about the government, administration, and police.

In the viral recording, a voice allegedly belonging to the OC is heard criticizing the Bangladesh Army, the police force, and the current administration.

The speaker in the clip also claimed that police personnel on the ground are 'very weak' and alleged that senior police officials were leaning towards the BNP.

Furthermore, the audio recording contains allegations of bribery within the police force, claiming that postings are secured through bribes.

Md Aktar Hossain, deputy commissioner (media) of the DMP, confirmed the withdrawal, stating it was done for 'administrative reasons'.

DMP officials have stated that the contents of the audio clip will be examined and further appropriate action will be taken against the OC if necessary.

#Bangladesh #Dhaka #Police #DMP #BreakingNews

Source: The Daily Star, Jamuna TV

headline_marked: BDR mutiny: [[Four witnesses allegedly shot and dumped in river]]
headline: BDR mutiny: Four witnesses allegedly shot and dumped in river
summary: Major Sabir testified at the International Crimes Tribunal-1 that RAB members killed four witnesses of the BDR mutiny under the orders of Ziaul Ahsan.
details: Major Sabir testified at the International Crimes Tribunal-1 on Thursday, stating that four witnesses of the BDR mutiny, including Nazrul Islam, were blindfolded, shot, and dumped into the Baleshwar River in cement bags.

The witness claimed that the killings took place in May 2010 under the direction and presence of Ziaul Ahsan, then head of the RAB Intelligence Wing, carried out by members of the RAB 8 Intelligence Wing.
According to the testimony, the victims were taken to the Baleshwar River in Patharghata's Charduniani on a fishing trawler with their faces and bodies covered.

Major Sabir also testified that another person was killed and dumped in the river in the same manner, and that a trawler driver named Alkas Majhi was disappeared and killed in 2011 during Ziaul Ahsan's 'golf operation'.
Former Army Chief Iqbal Karim Bhuiyan and other army and RAB officers have already testified against Ziaul Ahsan in this disappearance case.
This is the first disappearance case in the last 16 years to reach its final stages of trial.

Major Sabir also testified that another person was killed and dumped in the river in the same manner, and that a trawler driver named Alkas Majhi was disappeared and killed in 2011 during Ziaul Ahsan's 'golf operation'.
